source.section: PDF p.16 Line 22 - Marriage penalty credit and Marriage Penalty Credit Worksheet lines 1-14; PDF p.17 qualified income; Form ND-1 line 22; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 115,750.00 + wages (person 1) 115,750.00 = 231,500.00. Federal taxable income = 231,500.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 200,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 200,000.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 200,000.00. Subtractions lines 5-16: none; line 17 = 0.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 200,000.00 - 0.00 = 200,000.00. Line 19 = 200,000.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (200,000.00 - 80,975.00) = 1.95% x 119,025.00 = 2,320.9875, to the cent 2,320.99; taxable income is 100,000 or more, so the form itself uses the schedule (PDF p.29). Lines 21-23 credits: Marriage Penalty Credit Worksheet (not in the projection, shown for the difference): line 1 200,000.00; line 3a 115,750.00, line 3b 115,750.00; line 4 115,750.00; line 5 15,750.00; line 6 100,000.00; line 7 Single schedule tax on line 6 = 1,004.7375; line 8 100,000.00; line 9 Single schedule tax on line 8 = 1,004.7375; line 10 joint schedule tax on line 1 = 2,320.9875; line 11 = 2,009.475; line 12 = 311.5125; line 13 312.00; line 14 credit = 311.5125, 311.51. The projection does not take it (not_modelled, warn_when always), so credits stay 0.00 and expected overstates the form's net tax by 311.51. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 2,320.99.
